title: Advanced Solid-State Lithium-Oxygen Battery
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Solid-state lithium oxygen batteries (LOBs) are known for their enhanced safety, higher electrochemical stability, and improved energy density compared to liquid-state LOBs. However, the investigation of solid-state LOBs is limited with little understanding of their discharge and charge processes. In this work, a polymer-based solid-state LOB is used to investigate the effect of discharge rate on lithium peroxide (Li
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ) formation, the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), and cycle performance. In contrast to liquid cells, we unexpectedly found that the size of Li
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    particles increased as discharge current density decreased. High discharge current densities facilitate higher ORR and OER efficiency, as Li
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    preferentially grows on existing particles rather than nucleating new ones at high discharge rate, reducing byproduct formation and enhancing Li
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    yield. Cathode impedance was found to increase with decreasing current density while anode impedance was found to increase with increasing current density, both contribute to a reduced cycle life of solid-state LOBs and an optimal middle-ground current density. This work provides fundamental insights into the electrochemical behavior of solid-state LOBs, offering a strategic framework for optimizing discharge conditions to enhance efficiency, stability, and cycle life in next-generation energy storage systems.
                  </jats:p>
